scoring_contract.intermediate_values: Integers between anchors interpolate within the same rubric. Do not imply measured precision beyond evidence.

statuses.numeric: A 0–10 integer is assessed; null means unknown/unassessed. Movie show-only fields are inapplicable and null.
statuses.presence: Use the explicit present/absent/unknown states; never collapse unknown into absence.

scoring_contract.omission: All declared keys are required. Missing keys are contract failures, not zeros or implicit negatives.
scoring_contract.confidence: No calibrated confidence or per-field evidence object is requested. Record assessment_basis honestly; controller-owned source/run records retain actual provenance.
scoring_contract.scope: Every assessment belongs to an explicit movie, whole-show, season, or episode scope with an as-of date and coverage statement.

intensity.10: Exceptionally strong or pervasive in the defined scope.
intensity.1: Supported trace under this rubric. Do not use 1 merely because a weak association is imaginable.

centrality.0: No narrative importance. The content may be absent or present without a meaningful role; use content_presence separately where covered. Zero alone never certifies absence.
centrality.10: Defining focus; removing it fundamentally changes the work.
centrality.1: Supported, very minor narrative importance; occurrence alone is insufficient. Zero means no narrative importance, not certified absence.

membership.0: Does not use the genre conventions.
membership.1: Supported trace under this rubric. Do not use 1 merely because a weak association is imaginable.

prominence.8: Prominent across much of the scope.
prominence.1: Supported trace under this rubric. Do not use 1 merely because a weak association is imaginable.

frequency.1: Supported trace under this rubric. Do not use 1 merely because a weak association is imaginable.

quality.10: Exceptional execution. Absence is not a zero-quality score.
quality.1: Very unsuccessful execution; not a default for unknown quality or absent craft.

suitability.0: Very poor fit under the stated assumptions.
suitability.10: Exceptionally strong fit. Not a universal audience verdict.

separate_dimensions: Genre membership is not subject presence.
Release era is not setting era.
Production origin is not depicted culture or influence.
Intended audience is not age suitability.
Aesthetic appearance does not establish production technique.
Content presence is not narrative importance: a present detail can have centrality zero. Unknown presence and unknown applicability remain explicit.
scoring_contract.advisory_absence: An absent advisory requires sufficient coverage of the relevant scope and version. Do not turn synopsis silence into absence.
scoring_contract.series_policy: Movie scopes require null for every show-only numeric field and facet. Whole-show assessments name covered seasons; no claims about unassessed later releases.

experience.adrenaline.definition: Excitement and visceral exhilaration during viewing.

experience.tension.definition: Suspense, dread, or anticipation of an uncertain outcome.

experience.fear.definition: Fright or horror experienced, independently of horror genre membership.

experience.perceived_threat.definition: Sense that characters face harm, including harm never shown.

experience.romantic_feeling.definition: Romantic affection or longing evoked in the viewer.

experience.sensuality.definition: Erotic atmosphere or sexual tension, independently of explicit sexual depiction.

experience.warmth.definition: Affectionate, kind, or emotionally welcoming tone.

experience.wholesomeness.definition: Reassurance through care, kindness, and emotional safety.

experience.wonder.definition: Awe, amazement, or fascination with discovery.

experience.pathos.definition: Acute pity, sorrow, or tragic emotional impact.

experience.uncanniness.definition: Unease from the strangely familiar or almost natural.

experience.catharsis.definition: Emotional release after accumulated tension or feeling.

experience.nostalgia.definition: Longing for a remembered or imagined past evoked by the work; not release age.

experience.hopefulness.definition: Optimistic outlook or belief in positive possibilities.

experience.emotional_intensity.definition: Overall strength of emotional engagement, regardless of positive or negative tone.

experience.stress.definition: Sustained pressure, discomfort, or anxiety experienced during viewing.

experience.uplift.definition: Encouragement, joy, or improved spirits evoked.

experience.thought_provocation.definition: Invitation to reflect on ideas, ethics, or interpretations beyond the immediate plot.

experience.playfulness.definition: Light, mischievous, or freely inventive tone.

experience.sentimentality.definition: Overt appeal to tender feelings and emotional attachment.

experience.emotional_restraint.definition: Understated expression and withholding of overt emotional display.

experience.bittersweetness.definition: Positive and painful feelings intertwined rather than merely appearing separately.

experience.absurdity.definition: Experience of incongruity, illogic, or strangeness, whether humorous or unsettling.

experience.escapism.definition: Immersion away from everyday concerns; not limited to fantasy settings.

experience.wish_fulfillment.definition: Invitation to imagine desired powers, relationships, status, or ways of life.

experience.tranquility.definition: Calm, restful or meditative feeling evoked; not merely absence of tension.

experience.indignation.definition: Moral outrage or righteous anger evoked in the viewer; distinct from anger depicted by characters.

experience.disgust.definition: Revulsion evoked, independently of comic gross-out, frightening threat or grotesque visual style.

humor.overall.definition: Overall amount and strength of comedy, independently of individual humor styles.

humor.situational.definition: Humor from circumstances, misunderstandings, and complications; no episodic-format requirement.

humor.wit_wordplay.definition: Humor from verbal cleverness, puns, or linguistic ambiguity.

humor.physical.definition: Humor from bodily action, slapstick, or visual physical mishaps.

humor.cringe.definition: Humor from embarrassment or uncomfortable social situations.

humor.absurdist.definition: Humor from nonsense, illogic, or bizarre juxtapositions.

humor.satire.definition: Humorous critique of institutions, behavior, or social conventions.

humor.parody.definition: Humorous imitation of a recognizable work, genre, or style.

humor.dark.definition: Humor about death, suffering, taboo, or tragedy.

humor.running_gags.definition: Recurring jokes whose repetition or variation creates humor.

humor.meta.definition: Humor about storytelling, production, audiences, or the work itself.

humor.deadpan.definition: Humor delivered with apparent seriousness or minimal emotional reaction.

humor.gross_out.definition: Humor relying on bodily fluids, disgust, or vulgar physical material.

themes.crime.definition: Criminal acts and their consequences as subject matter.

themes.mystery.definition: Uncovering an important unknown as a central concern.

themes.war.definition: Armed conflict and its human or societal consequences.

themes.politics.definition: Governance, political institutions, and struggles for political power.

themes.radicalization.definition: A process of adopting increasingly extreme ideological commitments or endorsing extremist action. Distinct from existing political beliefs, ordinary persuasion, rebellion, group secrecy, and coercive group control; those alone do not establish radicalization.

themes.family.definition: Family bonds, conflict, obligations, and belonging.

themes.psychology.definition: Mental processes, internal conflict, or perception as subject matter.

themes.entertainment_industry.definition: The business and practice of entertainment and celebrity.

themes.social_critique.definition: Examination or criticism of social arrangements and norms.

themes.class.definition: Social class, economic inequality, and mobility.

themes.capitalism.definition: Economic systems organized around capital, profit, and ownership.

themes.consumerism.definition: Exploration or critique of acquiring goods, consumption, brands, or possessions as a source of identity, status, or fulfillment. Distinct from capitalism as an economic system; buying or using a product alone is insufficient.

themes.technological_change.definition: Exploration of societal or personal effects of technological development, adoption, or displacement, including effects on work, relationships, institutions, and identity. Gadget presence, advanced technology, or science alone is insufficient.

themes.human_nature.definition: Explicit thematic exploration of what humans are like: capacities, impulses, morality, cooperation, cruelty, or tensions between nature and social conditioning. Ordinary human characters, emotion, or drama alone is insufficient; not a synonym for personal identity, consciousness, or existential meaning.

themes.faith_and_spirituality.definition: Religious belief, spiritual practice, or metaphysical meaning.

themes.business.definition: Commercial organizations, enterprise, and work decisions.

themes.finance.definition: Money management, financial systems, investing, or debt.

themes.environment.definition: Relationships between human activity and ecosystems.

themes.science.definition: Scientific inquiry and its ideas, practice, or consequences.

themes.popular_culture.definition: Popular media, celebrity, fandom, or shared cultural trends.

themes.survival.definition: Meeting essential needs or overcoming threats to continued life.

themes.adventure.definition: Exploration, risk, and discovery outside ordinary life.

themes.hacking.definition: Intrusion into or manipulation of computer systems.

themes.artificial_intelligence.definition: Artificial agents and their interaction with the world.

themes.consciousness.definition: The nature of subjective experience and personhood.

themes.identity.definition: Formation, discovery, concealment, or change of personal identity.

themes.existential_meaning.definition: Purpose, freedom, mortality, and the meaning of existence.

themes.trauma.definition: Lasting effects of overwhelming or harmful experiences.

themes.recovery.definition: Processes of rebuilding after trauma, illness, or crisis.

themes.mental_health.definition: Mental health conditions, care, and lived experience.

themes.addiction.definition: Dependency and its effects on people and relationships.

themes.addiction_recovery.definition: Attempts to overcome dependency and maintain recovery.

themes.trust_and_betrayal.definition: Reliance on others, deception, and broken trust.

themes.coming_of_age.definition: Development toward adult identity, agency, or responsibility.

themes.coming_out.definition: Disclosure or recognition of LGBTQ identity in a social context.

themes.sexuality.definition: Sexual identity, desire, and their social meaning.

themes.gender_identity.definition: Gender identity and its personal or social implications. Distinct from social expectations about gender roles and from sexism; do not infer identity from conformity to or rejection of a role.

themes.gender_roles.definition: Exploration of social expectations, norms, or performances of masculinity, femininity, and gendered roles. Distinct from a person's gender identity and from sexism as discrimination; either may coexist without implying the other.

themes.immigration.definition: Migration across borders and the experience of settlement.

themes.displacement.definition: Loss of home or community through conflict, coercion, or other forces.

themes.gentrification.definition: Neighborhood change associated with investment and displacement.

themes.surveillance.definition: Monitoring, privacy, and control through observation.

themes.disease_and_pandemics.definition: Population-level disease transmission, epidemics, pandemics or public-health response matter as subjects. Personal diagnosis, dying and care are assessed separately as illness_and_dying.

themes.climate_change.definition: Climate processes, human causes, or consequences.

themes.inherited_wealth.definition: Inheritance, dynastic wealth, and intergenerational economic advantage.

themes.social_media.definition: Online social platforms and their effects on life.

themes.public_shaming.definition: Public condemnation, reputational punishment, or social exclusion.

themes.forgiveness.definition: Letting go of blame or reconciling after harm.

themes.loyalty.definition: Commitment to people, groups, or principles under pressure.

themes.belonging.definition: Acceptance, community, and finding a place among others.

themes.loneliness.definition: Isolation and unmet desire for connection.

themes.ambition.definition: Pursuit of achievement, status, or recognition.

themes.labor.definition: Working conditions, worker identity, organizing, and exploitation.

themes.colonialism.definition: Colonial domination, resistance, and its legacies.

themes.racism.definition: Racial discrimination and its personal or structural consequences.

themes.sexism.definition: Discrimination or domination based on sex or gender.

themes.caregiving.definition: Responsibility for another person's everyday support and wellbeing.

themes.parenthood.definition: Becoming or being a parent and its consequences.

themes.aging.definition: Later life, changing capacities, and social experiences of aging.

themes.midlife.definition: Reassessment and transitions in middle adulthood.

themes.retirement.definition: Leaving paid work and adjusting to life afterward.

themes.early_adulthood.definition: Independence, work, and relationships in early adult life.

themes.artistic_creation.definition: Making art and the motivations or struggles involved.

themes.persuasion_and_propaganda.definition: Shaping public or interpersonal belief through persuasion, spin, PR, advertising, propaganda or disinformation is a subject of the work; do not label the work itself propaganda from this score.

themes.illness_and_dying.definition: Personal illness, diagnosis, living with illness, dying or end-of-life care is a subject; distinct from population-level epidemics.

themes.corruption.definition: Abuse of entrusted public, organizational or professional power for private gain is a subject; not all crime or ambition is corruption.

narrative_engines.investigation.definition: Characters gather evidence to explain an event or identify responsibility.

narrative_engines.pursuit.definition: An extended chase or hunt organizes the story.

narrative_engines.rescue.definition: Saving someone from captivity or danger organizes the story.

narrative_engines.escape.definition: Getting out of confinement or an unsafe situation organizes the story.

narrative_engines.quest.definition: A journey toward a defined objective organizes the story.

narrative_engines.competition.definition: A contest with rivals and an outcome organizes the story.

narrative_engines.relationship_developme.definition: Changes in a relationship organize the story.

narrative_engines.everyday_life.definition: Ordinary routines and small events organize the story.

narrative_engines.survival.definition: Remaining alive under threatening conditions organizes the story.

narrative_engines.heist.definition: Planning, carrying out, or dealing with a theft organizes the story.

narrative_engines.espionage.definition: Secret intelligence gathering or covert state operations organize the story.

narrative_engines.military_operation.definition: An organized military mission structures the story.

narrative_engines.legal_case.definition: Court proceedings, formal adjudication or preparation for a legal case organize the story. Legislative debate or a political committee hearing alone belongs to political_struggle.

narrative_engines.political_struggle.definition: Pursuit or exercise of political power structures the story.

tropes.underdog_rise.definition: An initially disadvantaged character gains standing or succeeds against stronger opposition.

tropes.revenge.definition: Retaliation for a perceived wrong drives an arc.

tropes.fall_from_grace.definition: A character loses status, reputation, or moral standing.

tropes.redemption.definition: A character attempts to make amends or change after wrongdoing.

relationships.romantic_development.definition: Formation or deepening of a romantic relationship matters to the story.

relationships.established_couple.definition: An ongoing romantic partnership matters to the story; former partners or separated co-parents alone belong to breakup_or_divorce or parent_child.

relationships.breakup_or_divorce.definition: Ending a partnership matters to the story.

relationships.partner_bereavement.definition: Loss of a romantic partner matters to the story.

relationships.love_triangle.definition: Competing romantic attachments among three people matter to the story.

relationships.forbidden_romance.definition: A romantic relationship faces a consequential social or institutional prohibition.

relationships.friendship.definition: Non-romantic bonds of friendship matter to the story.

relationships.mentor_mentee.definition: Guidance and learning between mentor and mentee matter to the story.

relationships.rivalry.definition: Competition or mutual opposition between characters matters to the story.

relationships.forced_proximity.definition: Circumstances oblige characters to remain close or share space.

relationships.adversaries_cooperate.definition: Characters with genuinely opposing goals cooperate in a consequential shared undertaking; friendly peers in different industries are not automatically adversaries.

relationships.found_family.definition: Chosen bonds serve a family-like role in the story.

relationships.family_conflict.definition: Sustained conflict or harmful dysfunction within a family matters to the story.

relationships.intergenerational.definition: Relationships across generations matter to the story.

relationships.generational_trauma.definition: Trauma transmitted or repeated across generations matters to the story.

relationships.parent_child.definition: The relationship between parent and child matters to the story.

relationships.siblings.definition: Sibling relationships matter to the story.

relationships.caregiver_dependent.definition: Care and dependence between characters matter to the story.

relationships.human_animal_companionship.definition: An emotional bond between a person and animal matters to the story.

relationships.coercive_relationship.definition: Manipulation, coercion, or control within an interpersonal relationship matters to the story. Systematic control of members by a group is assessed separately as coercive_group_control; neither automatically implies the other.

relationships.coercive_group_control.definition: A group or leader systematically controls members through intimidation, isolation, dependency, punishment, or suppression of autonomy. Distinct from interpersonal coercion, voluntary discipline, secrecy, and radicalization; any of these may coexist but does not imply group control.
relationships.coercive_group_control.presence_definition: A group or leader systematically controls members through intimidation, isolation, dependency, punishment, or suppression of autonomy. Distinct from interpersonal coercion, voluntary discipline, secrecy, and radicalization; any of these may coexist but does not imply group control.

characters.ensemble.definition: Several focal characters share narrative attention and agency.

characters.antihero.definition: A focal character departs substantially from conventional heroic ethics or behavior.

characters.morally_ambiguous_cast.definition: Moral ambiguity among multiple major characters matters to the work.

characters.transformation_arc.definition: Substantial change in a focal character's beliefs, identity, or behavior.

characters.intellectual_problem_solver.definition: A focal character's reasoning or specialized intellectual ability drives events.

characters.detective_lead.definition: A focal character acts as an investigator or detective.

characters.workplace_team.definition: A team formed through work is a central social unit.

characters.family_business.definition: A family-run business is a central social unit.

characters.unaccompanied_children.definition: Children without their usual caregivers form a central social situation.

characters.teen_peer_group.definition: Teenage friendships and peer-group dynamics form a central social situation.

characters.clandestine_groups.definition: A secret society or organized group whose membership, meetings, activities, or aims are deliberately concealed. Secrecy is the defining feature, not coercion or extremist ideology; a secret held by one person, an ordinary private friendship, or crime alone is insufficient.
characters.clandestine_groups.presence_definition: A secret society or organized group whose membership, meetings, activities, or aims are deliberately concealed. Secrecy is the defining feature, not coercion or extremist ideology; a secret held by one person, an ordinary private friendship, or crime alone is insufficient.

world.advanced_technology.definition: Technology substantially beyond the work's contemporary baseline shapes its world.
world.advanced_technology.presence_definition: Technology substantially beyond the work's contemporary baseline occurs in its world.

world.magic.definition: Supernatural abilities or forces understood as magic shape the world.
world.magic.presence_definition: Supernatural abilities or forces understood as magic occur.

world.simulation.definition: An artificial simulation is an important layer of depicted reality. A physically staged real environment or social deception alone is not a simulation.
world.simulation.presence_definition: An artificial simulation is presented as a layer of reality.

world.virtual_reality.definition: Characters experience an interactive digitally mediated environment. A physical set, surveillance broadcast or deception alone is not virtual reality.
world.virtual_reality.presence_definition: Characters experience an interactive digitally mediated environment.

world.parallel_worlds.definition: Coexisting alternative realities matter to the world.

world.time_travel.definition: Movement across time outside ordinary chronological passage matters to the world.
world.time_travel.presence_definition: Movement across time outside ordinary chronological passage occurs.

world.time_loop.definition: Repetition of a period of time matters to the world or narrative.
world.time_loop.presence_definition: A period of time repeats within the story world.

world.dystopian_society.definition: Oppressive or deeply dysfunctional social arrangements define the world.
world.dystopian_society.presence_definition: An oppressive or deeply dysfunctional society is depicted.

world.post_apocalyptic.definition: Life after a civilization-scale catastrophe defines the world.
world.post_apocalyptic.presence_definition: Life after a civilization-scale catastrophe is depicted.

world.spacefaring.definition: Travel or life beyond Earth is consequential to the world.
world.spacefaring.presence_definition: Travel or life beyond Earth occurs.

world.robots.definition: Embodied artificial machines functioning as agents matter to the world; not synonymous with AI.
world.robots.presence_definition: Embodied artificial machines functioning as agents occur; AI without embodiment is insufficient.

world.myth_and_folklore.definition: Recognizable mythological or folkloric traditions shape the world.
world.myth_and_folklore.presence_definition: Recognizable mythological or folkloric beings, events, or practices occur in the story world; a passing idiom is insufficient.

world_treatment.scientific_rigor.definition: Attention to scientific constraints and explanatory consistency; not an inverse of speculative freedom.

world_treatment.speculative_freedom.definition: Freedom to use speculative premises without scientific elaboration.

world_treatment.worldbuilding_depth.definition: Detail and interconnection in the world's institutions, history, and rules.

world_treatment.magic_rule_detail.definition: Elaboration of rules and constraints governing magic.

world_treatment.everyday_realism.definition: Attention to plausible ordinary behavior and material conditions, independently of era.

world_treatment.magical_realism.definition: Impossible or supernatural events are treated as ordinary within an otherwise everyday world; distinct from an explicitly elaborated magic system.

storytelling.plot_velocity.definition: Rate at which consequential plot events occur.

storytelling.gradual_development.definition: Deliberate accumulation of character, relationships, or tension over time; can coexist with rapid action.

storytelling.intrigue.definition: Strength of curiosity about what happens or what is concealed.

storytelling.plot_complexity.definition: Interdependence of events, causes, and plot threads.

storytelling.interpretive_ambiguity.definition: Extent to which meaning or events support multiple interpretations.

storytelling.twist_frequency.definition: Recurrence of major reversals or revelations over the work.

storytelling.twist_impact.definition: Extent to which revelations alter understanding or expectations.

storytelling.multiple_timelines.definition: Use of distinct temporal strands; not necessarily time travel.

storytelling.multiple_viewpoints.definition: Distribution of storytelling across distinct character perspectives.

storytelling.unreliable_narration.definition: Uncertainty created by an unreliable narrator or viewpoint.

storytelling.unreliable_reality.definition: Uncertainty about which presented events or reality layers are real.

storytelling.self_reference.definition: Attention to the work's own storytelling or construction.

storytelling.fourth_wall_breaking.definition: Explicit acknowledgment of the audience or of the work as a presented fiction, including direct address. Voiceover alone is not sufficient.

storytelling.voiceover.definition: Use of spoken narration over images outside ordinary scene dialogue.

storytelling.dream_sequences.definition: Use of dreams or hallucinations as presented sequences.

storytelling.observational_mode.definition: Attention to behavior and environments without strong explanatory or plot intervention.

storytelling.slice_of_life.definition: Emphasis on ordinary experience rather than extraordinary plot escalation.

storytelling.exposition_load.definition: Amount of explanatory information the viewer must absorb.

storytelling.information_withholding.definition: Deliberate delay in supplying information needed to understand events.

storytelling.formal_challenge.definition: Departure from familiar formal conventions that demands adaptation.

storytelling.didacticism.definition: How explicitly the work states, teaches or argues a message; independent of intellectual stimulation or whether the viewer agrees.

storytelling.confined_setting.definition: Concentration of the work within a single location or tightly bounded connected spaces; distinct from small cast, low budget or confinement as a plot event.

stakes.personal.definition: Consequences for an individual's life, identity, or goals.

stakes.relationship.definition: Consequences for a central relationship or small social unit.

stakes.community.definition: Consequences for a locality or community.

stakes.societal.definition: Consequences for institutions, a society, or civilization.

stakes.urgency.definition: Time pressure on consequential decisions or events.

dialogue.density.definition: Amount of spoken dialogue relative to the work's running time.

dialogue.dependence.definition: Importance of understanding dialogue to follow the work.

dialogue.overlap.definition: Use of simultaneous or overlapping speech.

dialogue.naturalistic_delivery.definition: Conversational delivery resembling spontaneous everyday speech.

dialogue.theatrical_delivery.definition: Heightened, rhetorical, or explicitly performative speech.

aesthetics.gothic.definition: Ominous, decaying, or romantically macabre visual atmosphere.

aesthetics.noir.definition: Shadowed, morally uneasy visual and atmospheric treatment, independently of crime plotting.

aesthetics.retro.definition: Deliberately retrospective visual or sonic styling; not merely an older release.

aesthetics.minimalism.definition: Reduction of visual, sonic, or formal elements.

aesthetics.stylization.definition: Departure from naturalistic presentation through a distinctive audiovisual treatment.

aesthetics.surrealism.definition: Dreamlike or illogical relationships in presented images and events.

aesthetics.psychedelia.definition: Hallucinatory, distorted, or perceptually altered sensory treatment.

aesthetics.grotesquerie.definition: Emphasis on distorted, repulsive, or biologically unsettling forms.

aesthetics.camp.definition: Theatrical excess and conspicuous artifice with an invitation to enjoy that excess.

aesthetics.ironic_distance.definition: Presentation that invites distance from its apparent surface meaning.

aesthetics.intimacy.definition: Presentation fostering closeness to characters' private experience.

aesthetics.spectacle.definition: Emphasis on impressive scale, effects, and set pieces.

aesthetics.immersion.definition: Strength of the sensory sense of inhabiting the work's world.

aesthetics.lyricism.definition: Poetic, associative presentation through image, language, sound or rhythm; not a synonym for slow pacing.

aesthetics.transgression.definition: Perceptible aesthetic treatment that deliberately challenges taboos or conventions; do not infer a creator's private intent or equate explicit content alone with transgression.

visuals.muted_palette.definition: Use of restrained or desaturated colors.

visuals.warm_color.definition: Prominence of warm hues and lighting.

visuals.cool_color.definition: Prominence of cool hues and lighting.

visuals.low_key_lighting.definition: Predominance of dark lighting with selective illumination.

visuals.high_key_lighting.definition: Predominance of bright, evenly illuminated scenes.

visuals.high_contrast.definition: Strong contrast between light and dark regions.

visuals.long_takes.definition: Prominence of extended shots without cuts; method of capture is irrelevant.

visuals.handheld_motion.definition: Prominence of visibly handheld or unstable camera movement.

visuals.production_design_detail.definition: Density of expressive detail in constructed environments and props.

visuals.cutting_pace.definition: Perceived rate of shot changes and editing transitions: 0 means virtually no cuts, not low quality. Distinct from rate of plot events.

action.martial_arts_choreography.definition: Combat organized around recognizable or stylized martial arts movement.

action.grappling.definition: Combat involving holds, clinches, throws, or ground fighting.

action.blade_combat.definition: Combat involving swords, knives, or similar blades.

action.superpowered_combat.definition: Combat involving abilities beyond ordinary human capacities.

action.large_battles.definition: Combat involving many participants or military-scale engagement.

action.gritty_combat.definition: Combat presented as physically punishing, messy, and effortful.

action.stylized_violence.definition: Violence presented through conspicuously aestheticized movement or imagery.

action.realistic_violence.definition: Violence presented with plausible physical consequences and vulnerability.

horror_modes.possession.definition: A supernatural entity inhabits or takes control of a person as a horror mechanism. Explicitly excludes psychological dissociation, an alternate personality without supernatural inhabitation, ordinary manipulation or influence, and merely owning or using a magical object.
horror_modes.possession.presence_definition: A supernatural entity inhabits or takes control of a person. Psychological dissociation, alternate personality without supernatural inhabitation, mere influence, and owning a magical object do not qualify.

horror_modes.body_horror.definition: Transformation, violation, or instability of the body matters to the horror.

horror_modes.folk_horror.definition: Folk belief, ritual, landscape, or insular tradition matters to the horror.

horror_modes.cosmic_horror.definition: Human insignificance before incomprehensible forces matters to the horror.

horror_modes.psychological_horror.definition: Perception, mental distress, or internal instability drives the horror.

sound.design_prominence.definition: Expressive prominence of non-musical sound design; not a quality judgment.

sound.ambient_soundscapes.definition: Use of environmental sound to create atmosphere.

sound.silence.definition: Expressive use of silence or near silence.

sound.sparse_score.definition: Use of little or no non-diegetic score.

sound.audio_startles.definition: Abrupt sound events intended to startle.

sound.music_dependence.definition: Importance of music to emotional or narrative understanding.

sound.musical_numbers.definition: Prominence of song or dance sequences functioning as narrative expression.

ending.conflict_resolution.definition: Extent to which central dramatic conflicts receive an outcome; independent of happiness.

ending.interpretive_openness.definition: Extent to which the ending permits multiple interpretations.

ending.emotional_closure.definition: Extent of emotional completion or release at the ending.

ending.happiness.definition: Positive emotional outcome for focal characters at the ending.

ending.tragedy.definition: Loss, defeat, or suffering defining the ending.

ending.bittersweetness.definition: Intertwined positive and painful outcomes at the ending.

viewing_demands.sensory_intensity.definition: Strength and density of audiovisual stimulation.
